name: Korah
bio:
Korah was a grandson of Kohath and son of Izhar, of the tribe of Levi. He joined with Dathan and Abiram of the tribe of Reuben, along with 250 well-known leaders of the congregation, to rise up against Moses and Aaron, demanding, "You have gone too far! ... Is it not enough that the LORD has set the whole community apart to himself? Why then do you set yourselves above the LORD's assembly?" (Numbers 16:1-3).

Moses proposed that the next day Korah's company each bring a censer and offer incense before the LORD, so the LORD himself would show who was holy and chosen. The next day Korah gathered the whole assembly at the entrance to the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD appeared to them all; the ground opened up and swallowed Korah, Dathan, Abiram, everyone who belonged to them, and all their households and possessions, while fire from the LORD consumed the 250 leaders who had offered incense (Numbers 16:16-35). Korah's rebellion became a lasting biblical warning against envying the priesthood and usurping authority God himself had appointed, and the New Testament book of Jude invokes "Korah's rebellion" as a warning against false teachers (Jude 11).
